The Federal Aviation Administration launched a federal electric vertical takeoff and landing pilot program in North Carolina, marking a significant step toward commercializing advanced air mobility in the United States. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy celebrated the initiative, which aims to transform how Americans move by leveraging the state’s aviation heritage [FAA launched the pilot program](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/trumps-transportation-secretary-sean-p-duffy-celebrates-launch-federal-evtol-pilot-0). This development coincides with the agency’s announcement of a major expansion to its BEYOND program, which will double in size by selecting up to eight additional entities to lead drone integration efforts into the national airspace system [FAA announced the expansion](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/trumps-transportation-secretary-sean-p-duffy-announces-major-expansion-faa-beyond-program). These simultaneous moves signal a coordinated federal strategy to accelerate the commercial deployment of both eVTOL aircraft and unmanned aerial systems.

In parallel, the Department of Transportation delivered $1.1 billion in funding to upgrade airport infrastructure, including a record $10.9 million investment to equip 3,000 runway vehicles with transmitters at 61 airports [FAA delivered the funding](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/trumps-transportation-secretary-sean-p-duffy-delivers-11-billion-upgrade-airports). The agency also introduced the SMART platform, a state-of-the-art air traffic control management tool that centralizes 200 data streams to improve airspace management and reduce flight delays [FAA delivered the tool](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/trumps-transportation-secretary-sean-p-duffy-delivers-state-art-air-traffic-control). These infrastructure investments support the broader goal of modernizing the aviation ecosystem to handle increased traffic from new aircraft types.

On the defense and security front, Leonardo DRS secured a $500 million ceiling counter-drone radar slot with a Pentagon task force, strengthening U.S. capabilities against advanced unmanned threats [Dealroom reported the contract](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitgFBVV95cUxPd0t1d2t4Mk9TcmZZRzRkSzM3d01TcjJpcWpyUW9yX1JUN3BXTnZtNkdwV04zLU9WeU1JQXRoS0ZrQ0xJb212d1hoUWs3bDN1OW13R3ZHX2hQNkxwT25fa293VTBlMXlUbzZIN3N4Tm9ZckNUbVk2UUVhaVRMNXVuOFdzWDFyQnlKOE8xZTZ0Z04zM3gyN0xVSExvV2FjX2ZJS1JLVE5KMU9GT2ExOG9peGR5Uk5wQQ?oc=5). Meanwhile, the U.S. Army enhanced Stryker combat units with counter-drone warfare systems on NATO’s eastern flank, reflecting a growing emphasis on integrated air defense [Army Recognition reported the deployment](https://news.google.?oc=5). These actions highlight a sustained trend of integrating counter-unmanned systems into both domestic and allied defense architectures.

In the autonomous vehicle sector, Tesla launched the Cybercab in Austin, while Pony.ai began testing its Gen-7 Robotaxi in Manchester, expanding its presence in the United Kingdom to two cities [Gasgoo reported the testing](https://news.google.?oc=5). Simultaneously, Waymo expanded its service to 20 cities as the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opened a new school bus safety probe, indicating continued regulatory scrutiny of autonomous operations [Startup Fortune reported the expansion](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMingFBVV95cUxPTGJublNHeG9KZDVRbFZIdzNad2w4ZTQzY01XcEJ2ZnJkRzM5NkdQZm9TZHNyTEZ6anhyemJPdU9kbnpKQUFLYWlWMVlxekRVUjZTaEpuOXpneGN3dFhvUHRRdTdEZkVJUGNMOXRDaWp2Y0k0SXNWQkFacEtwU0h6SXIzTzVtUktMdjZCRkVITFlVWmJMQ0lEZVRKWGhCdw?oc=5).
